headline_en: Boat sinks off Teknaf coast on the way from Myanmar to Malaysia; Rohingya mother and son die
summary_en: A boat carrying irregular migrants from Myanmar's Rakhine state capsized off Baharchhara, Teknaf (Cox's Bazar) at dawn on Tuesday 22 September 2026. A Rohingya woman and her 9-year-old son died, 16 people were rescued alive and one woman was missing. Eight of the rescued are Bangladeshis who say they were taken to Myanmar about a year earlier on a promise of being sent to Malaysia and were held there for a year.

facts.statement: A boat full of irregular migrants coming from Myanmar sank at dawn on Tuesday (22 September 2026) off the Boro Dail-Kachchhapia boat landing in Baharchhara union, Teknaf, Cox's Bazar; the Bangladesh Coast Guard recovered the bodies of a Rohingya woman, Chhura Khatun (28), and her 9-year-old son.

In the Teknaf boat sinking, 16 people were rescued alive by the Coast Guard and local residents (13 men, 2 women and 1 child according to police), and one woman was still missing as of Wednesday afternoon, 23 September 2026.
facts.source_in_article: Coast Guard; Inspector Md. Abu Sayed, in-charge of Baharchhara police investigation centre

facts.statement: The boat travelled from Myanmar's Rakhine state across the Naf river and the Bay of Bengal to the Baharchhara coast of Teknaf, where a large wave overturned it late at night as it was entering via the Baharchhara boat landing.

Eight Bangladeshis among those rescued told police they were taken from Bangladesh to Myanmar about a year earlier on the promise of being taken on to Malaysia; instead of being sent to Malaysia they were kept in various places in Myanmar for the past year.

According to police citing the rescued people, on Monday night (21 September 2026) they were put on a boat to be sent to Malaysia by sea and brought to the Baharchhara coast of Teknaf, where the boat sank after being hit by a wave.

The rescued Bangladeshis are Omar Faruk of ward 9 of Teknaf municipality; Kurban Ali of Majher Para, Shahporir Dwip, Sabrang union; Abu Rasel and Jamir Hossain of Naikhongchhari; Md. Mostafa of Katakhali, Hoaikyong, Teknaf; Abdul Kader of Uttar Nengulbil, Teknaf Sadar union; Mizanur Rahman of Morichya Ghona; and Apu Barua of Rajapalong union, Ukhiya.

Most of the Rohingya on the boat are reported to be registered residents of the Teknaf and Ukhiya refugee camps. The rescued Rohingya named are Md. Salim (Mochni camp, Hnila, Teknaf), Md. Hossain (Kutupalong camp, Ukhiya), Md. Saiful Karim (Akyab, Myanmar), Abdul Amin (Teknaf camp-26), Samjida (Chakmarkul camp-21, Hoaikyong), Lal Moti of Buthidaung, Rakhine and her 9-year-old son Hossain Johar, and Md. Idris (Jadimura camp-27).

The 16 people rescued were handed over to Teknaf Model police station at night; police were verifying their identities and said necessary action would be taken. The total number on the boat and the identity of the missing woman were not known.
facts.source_in_article: Saiful Islam, officer-in-charge (OC) of Teknaf Model Thana

headline_en: Remittances in August close to 3 billion dollars
summary_en: Bangladesh Bank's monthly figures published on 1 September 2026 show remittances of USD 297.66 crore in August 2026, 22.50% more than a year earlier. July-August of fiscal year 2026-27 totalled USD 582.53 crore, and fiscal 2025-26 set a record of USD 3,559 crore.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 297 crore 66 lakh in remittances in August 2026, the second month of fiscal year 2026-27, which is 22.50% more than the same period of the previous fiscal year.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladesh Bank monthly data published 1 September 2026

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 286 crore 87 lakh in remittances in July 2026; July-August of fiscal 2026-27 together brought USD 582 crore 53 lakh, about 20% more than the same period of the previous fiscal year.
In fiscal year 2025-26 expatriates sent a record total of USD 3,559 crore in remittances; in six of the twelve months remittances exceeded USD 300 crore.
In fiscal year 2024-25 remittances through banks grew by about 27% and exceeded USD 30 billion for the first time, after a sudden jump following the political change two years before September 2026.
The highest remittance of any single month was USD 375 crore 22 lakh in March 2026; the second highest was USD 342 crore 50 lakh in May 2026.
Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves stood at USD 3,740 crore on Tuesday 1 September 2026; under the IMF's BPM6 method the reserves were USD 3,249 crore.

headline_en: USD 215 crore in remittances arrived in 22 days
summary_en: In the first 22 days of June 2026 Bangladesh received USD 215 crore in remittances, 1.8% more than the same days of June 2025. Remittances had exceeded USD 3 billion for six months in a row since December 2025, with Islami Bank and Bangladesh Krishi Bank the top collectors.

facts.statement: In the first 22 days of June 2026 Bangladesh received USD 2.15 billion (215 crore) in remittances, equal to BDT 26,230 crore; in the first 22 days of June 2025 it was USD 211 crore, so growth was 1.8%.

Remittances exceeded USD 3 billion (300 crore) for six consecutive months from December 2025: December USD 322 crore, January 2026 USD 317 crore, February USD 302 crore, March about USD 375 crore, April USD 312 crore 70 lakh, May USD 342 crore 50 lakh (May was 15.34% above May 2025).
Islami Bank is top in collecting remittances, followed by Bangladesh Krishi Bank (BKB).

People in the banking sector said expatriate Bangladeshis sent more money in March and April 2026 because of Eid-ul-Fitr and the war of the United States and Israel with Iran in the Middle East, and the trend continued in May ahead of Eid-ul-Azha.
In the 11 months July-May of fiscal 2025-26 Bangladesh received USD 3,275 crore 68 lakh in remittances, more than 19% above the USD 2,750 crore 69 lakh of the same period a year earlier.

headline_en: Taken to Kazakhstan on a promise of Australia and tortured: how Sohel got back
summary_en: Sohel Rana alias Jewel (38) of Bagharpara, Jashore, gave up his restaurant business in Malaysia on a broker's promise of Europe, then agreed to go to Australia for BDT 16 lakh and paid BDT 12 lakh. He was flown via Dubai to Kazakhstan in January 2026, had his passport taken, was confined in an iron-smelting factory and asked for BDT 30 lakh, escaped, and came home on a travel permit on 20 April 2026 after his wife sent a further BDT 2.2 lakh. A trafficking case against the broker couple Md. Kaiyum and Nazma Akter was recorded on 6 April 2026; no one has been arrested.

facts.statement: Sohel Rana alias Jewel (38) of Ghop Durgapur village, Bagharpara upazila, Jashore, left Bangladesh for Australia on 15 January 2026 under a BDT 16 lakh contract; he had paid BDT 12 lakh to the broker from his savings, money borrowed against a promise to give paddy instead of interest, an NGO loan and other borrowing.
The broker Nazma Akter agreed to send Sohel Rana to Australia on the condition of a job paying USD 1,000 a month; after taking the money she kept stalling him.

Sohel Rana met broker Nazma Akter alias Nurjahan in 2014 in Bangladesh; she lured him with a promise of sending him to Europe within three to four months, so he returned from Malaysia in November 2024 (leaving two restaurants he had built there after going in December 2016 as a hotel cook), but she could not send him to Europe and then offered Australia.

Sohel Rana was first taken on 15 January 2026 to Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on a one-month business visa, and the next day, 16 January, to Kazakhstan, where he was told he would be taken to Australia after staying one month.

In Kazakhstan the abuse began at the hotel; the broker Nazma's representative took the passports of Sohel and two other Bangladeshis, and on 24 January 2026 they were driven about 900 km to a hilly area named Shimkyat (শিমক্যাট) and locked in an iron-smelting factory, given one piece of bread once a day.
The broker's representative demanded BDT 30 lakh from Sohel Rana and two other Bangladeshis to be let out of the factory in Kazakhstan where they were held, and threatened to kill them otherwise.

On 28 January 2026 Sohel Rana and one of the two other captive Bangladeshis escaped over the factory boundary wall with the help of a guard; the third Bangladeshi did not agree to escape. They then stayed in a hotel.
On 14 April 2026 Sohel Rana and his companion sent a text message to the mobile phone of a Bangladesh immigration officer describing their danger.

A South African lawyer demanded BDT 1 lakh 20 thousand to send Sohel Rana home from Kazakhstan; Sohel's wife borrowed and sent the lawyer BDT 1 lakh 20 thousand plus another BDT 1 lakh for the air fare, and Sohel returned to Bangladesh on 20 April 2026 with a travel permit.

Sohel's wife Mukta Begum applied on 9 March 2026 to the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Prevention and Suppression Tribunal-1, Jashore, for a case; on the court's order the case was recorded at Bagharpara police station on 6 April 2026 against Md. Kaiyum (48) of Muslimnagar village, Keraniganj upazila, Dhaka, and his wife Nazma Akter (45). Police had not arrested anyone as of 22 June 2026.

The investigating officer, Sub-Inspector Md. Mizanur Rahman of Bagharpara police station, said accused Md. Kaiyum is outside the country and efforts are on to arrest the other accused, Nazma Akter; Nazma Akter's phone was found switched off on repeated calls by the reporter.
facts.source_in_article: SI Md. Mizanur Rahman, Bagharpara Thana

facts.statement: After returning on 20 April 2026 Sohel Rana says he has about BDT 15 lakh of debt and nothing left but his homestead; creditors come to his house daily and he sometimes stays in hiding. He wants the money returned.

headline_en: More than three billion dollars in remittances for six months running
summary_en: Bangladesh Bank data published on 1 June 2026 show remittances of USD 342.5 crore in May 2026, 15.34% up on May 2025, making six consecutive months above USD 3 billion. The article gives bank-wise figures for May and the reserve position.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 342 crore 50 lakh 30 thousand in remittances in May 2026, 15.34% more than the USD 296 crore 94 lakh 60 thousand of May 2025.

Monthly remittances were USD 322 crore in December 2025, 317 crore in January 2026, 302 crore in February, about 375 crore in March, 312 crore 70 lakh in April and 342.5 crore in May, six straight months above USD 300 crore.

Banking sector people said expatriates sent more money in March and April 2026 because of Eid-ul-Fitr and the US-Israel war with Iran, and in May ahead of Eid-ul-Azha; because of the Middle East crisis the taka had weakened somewhat against the dollar, so remitters were getting a higher price per dollar.
In July-May of fiscal 2025-26 Bangladesh received USD 3,275 crore 68 lakh in remittances, more than 19% above the USD 2,750 crore 69 lakh of the first 11 months of the previous fiscal year.
In May 2026 private banks brought about USD 238 crore 67 lakh in remittances; Islami Bank alone brought about USD 59 crore 21 lakh and BRAC Bank, second among private banks, about USD 41 crore.

In May 2026 the six state-owned banks brought about USD 56 crore 65 lakh in remittances, of which Agrani Bank brought the most, about USD 24.25 crore; the specialised Krishi Bank brought about USD 47 crore and is second overall.
On Monday 1 June 2026 Bangladesh's gross foreign exchange reserves were USD 3,477 crore (34.77 billion); under the IMF BPM6 method USD 3,011 crore (30.11 billion).

headline_en: Bangladeshis in Korea demand an Incheon transit on the Dhaka-Tokyo route
summary_en: Bangladeshis living in South Korea welcomed Biman Bangladesh Airlines' plan to restart direct Dhaka-Tokyo flights in June 2026 and demanded a short transit or stopover at Incheon International Airport on that route. Because there is no direct Dhaka-Korea flight, they travel via third countries at higher fares and longer times; they have opened an online petition portal.

facts.statement: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has taken an initiative to restart its direct Dhaka-Tokyo flight in June 2026.

There is no direct Dhaka-Korea flight, so Bangladeshi expatriates mostly have to travel through a third country, which takes more time, costs comparatively higher fares and often creates transit complications; passengers have to use various foreign airlines.

Bangladeshis in South Korea are demanding that Biman add a short transit or stopover at Incheon International Airport on the Dhaka-Tokyo route, so passengers could travel Dhaka-Incheon-Tokyo or Incheon-Dhaka.

Korea-based Bangladeshis launched an online opinion and petition web portal, https://petition2biman.com, where Bangladeshis living in Korea, people travelling between Bangladesh and Korea and future users of the route can join the petition by giving some basic information.

The expatriate community called on the Bangladesh Embassy in Seoul, Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism and government policymakers to act quickly, and asked people to tag Biman and the Bangladesh Embassy Seoul in an online campaign.

The article says a large number of Bangladeshi workers, students, businesspeople, researchers and professionals live in South Korea, and many workers, students and businesspeople plan to go there from Bangladesh every year.

headline_en: UK sanctions a Bangladeshi company over human trafficking to Russia
summary_en: On Tuesday 5 May 2026 the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office announced sanctions, including an asset freeze, on the Bangladeshi travel company Dream Home Travels and Tours Limited of Banani, Dhaka, under the UK's Global Irregular Migration and Trafficking in Persons Sanctions Regulations 2025. The UK says the company advertised high-paid service-sector jobs in Russia and that the Bangladeshis recruited were forced to fight on the front line against Ukraine.

facts.statement: On Tuesday 5 May 2026 the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office announced sanctions on a Bangladeshi travel company, Dream Home Travels and Tours Limited, under the UK's Global Irregular Migration and Trafficking in Persons Sanctions Regulations 2025; the announcement was published on the UK government website and the measures include an asset freeze.
facts.source_in_article: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office notice

facts.statement: The UK sanctions document gives the address of Dream Home Travels and Tours Limited as a house in Banani, Dhaka; the company is number 5 on a list of 17 individuals and entities from several countries.

According to the UK government, Dream Home Travels and Tours Limited recruited Bangladeshi citizens by deception and then exploited them: it advertised high-paid jobs in Russia's service sector, but after the Bangladeshis reached Russia they were forced to fight on the front line of Russia's war against Ukraine.

The UK's stated reason is that there are reasonable grounds to suspect Dream Home Travels and Tours Limited is an involved entity under the 2025 regulations because it is or has been involved in human trafficking activity.

headline_en: Record remittances: USD 375 crore in March
summary_en: March 2026 set a new monthly remittance record of USD 3.75 billion, 14% above the previous record of March 2025, driven by Eid and the US-Israel war with Iran in the Middle East. Economists advised Bangladesh Bank to hold on to its reserves; a Bangladesh Bank report says half of all remittances come from the six Gulf countries.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 3.75 billion (375 crore) in remittances in March 2026, the highest ever for a single month and 14% more than March 2025.
The previous record month was March 2025 with USD 329 crore 56 lakh 30 thousand; the third highest was December 2025 with USD 322 crore 66 lakh and the fourth January 2026 with USD 317 crore.

The article says expatriates sent more money in March 2026 because of the Ramadan Eid and the war of the United States and Israel with Iran in the Middle East; although the war had intensified, the pace of remittances was still satisfactory.
Because of the Middle East crisis the dollar exchange rate against the taka had risen, so dollars sent as remittance were fetching a higher price.

A recent Bangladesh Bank report on remittances shows that half of Bangladesh's total remittances come from the six oil-rich Gulf countries: Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and Kuwait.

Eight noted economists, at a recent meeting with Bangladesh Bank, advised it to hold on to foreign exchange reserves to absorb a possible shock from the Middle East war, not to cut the policy interest rate yet, to find alternative energy sources to the Middle East, and not to pass higher world prices to consumers immediately.
facts.source_in_article: eight economists (unnamed) at a meeting with Bangladesh Bank

key_quote_bn: তেলসমৃদ্ধ ছয়টি উপসাগরীয় দেশ সৌদি আরব, সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাত (ইউএই), কাতার, ওমান, বাহরাইন ও কুয়েত থেকেই আসে মোট প্রবাসী আয়ের অর্ধেক।

headline_en: Uncertainty from the Middle East crisis: what should remittance-dependent families do
summary_en: A personal-finance piece advising families in Bangladesh who depend on remittances from the Middle East to prepare for a possible fall in income during the regional unrest. It lists five steps: review spending, build an emergency fund, reduce dependence on one income source, cut high-interest debt and divide a returning migrant's lump-sum savings.

facts.statement: Families dependent on remittances are advised to separate fixed and non-fixed spending, treat rent, education and medicine as priorities, postpone travel, festivals and unnecessary purchases, and work out the minimum cost of at least three months.
facts.source_in_article: the article (Prothom Alo personal finance desk)

facts.statement: Remittance-receiving families are advised to build a separate emergency fund equal to three to six months of expenses; if that is not possible at once, set aside 10 to 15% of the remittance in a separate bank account or short-term savings certificates (sanchayapatra).

The article's worked example: a family receiving BDT 50,000 a month in remittance with minimum spending of BDT 35,000 can target an emergency fund of at least BDT 1 lakh 5 thousand (three months' spending), reachable in one year by setting aside BDT 7,000 a month.

Families are advised to reduce total dependence on remittance by having another member earn part-time (work from home, small business, skill-based services) and to plan to pay off high-interest personal loans or credit cards first.

Keeping the risk of the migrant having to return in mind, the article advises not spending a migrant's lump-sum savings all at once but dividing it: one part emergency fund, one part income-generating investment, the rest in safe deposits.

The article says that when employment, wages or working hours fall in the Middle East it directly affects the cash flow of families in Bangladesh, and families relying solely on remittance are at comparatively higher risk; there is no certainty when the Middle East situation will normalise.
facts.source_in_article: the article, citing a review of Bangladesh Bank data

headline_en: Remittances topped 3 billion dollars in February too
summary_en: Bangladesh received USD 302 crore in remittances in February 2026, 19.15% above February 2025, the third month running above USD 3 billion though lower than January and December. Bank officials linked recent strength to the election and to reduced hundi.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 3.02 billion (302 crore) in remittances in February 2026, 19.15% more than the USD 2.52 billion (252 crore) of February 2025, an increase of USD 49 crore 30 lakh.

In the first eight months (July-February) of fiscal 2025-26 Bangladesh received USD 22.45 billion (2,245 crore) in remittances, against USD 18.49 billion (1,849 crore) in the same period of fiscal 2024-25.

Remittances were USD 322 crore in December 2025, 317 crore in January 2026 and 302 crore in February 2026, falling month to month; in the five months before December 2025 they were below USD 3 billion each month.

Several bank officials, speaking anonymously, said remittances usually rise before the two Eids, but over the last two to three months the pace was good because of the recently held election; funds raised from Bangladeshis abroad for many candidates later came into the country as remittance.

In calendar 2025 Bangladesh received USD 3,282 crore in remittances in total, about equal to Bangladesh Bank's foreign exchange reserves; the record single month then was USD 329 crore in March 2025 (ahead of Eid-ul-Fitr) and December 2025's USD 322 crore was the second highest.

Banking sector people said illegal hundi business has fallen because money laundering has fallen, and the dollar exchange rate in the banking channel has been stable for several months, so more remittance is coming by legal channels.

headline_en: USD 181 crore in remittances in 16 days; reserves rise to USD 3,453 crore
summary_en: In the first 16 days of February 2026 Bangladesh received USD 180.7 crore in remittances, 21% up on a year earlier, and gross reserves rose to USD 34.53 billion as Bangladesh Bank kept buying dollars from banks. Bank officials attributed the two-month rise mainly to the election.

facts.statement: In the first 16 days of February 2026 Bangladesh received USD 180 crore 70 lakh in remittances, 21% more than the USD 149 crore of 1-16 February 2025; USD 15 crore 20 lakh came on 16 February alone.

Bangladesh Bank's gross foreign exchange reserves rose to USD 34.53 billion on Tuesday 17 February 2026 (USD 29.85 billion under IMF BPM6); on 7 February they were USD 34.06 billion (BPM6: 29.47 billion). Bangladesh Bank has been buying dollars from banks as remittances grow.

Ahead of the election expatriates sent on average USD 11 crore 25 lakh a day in February 2026; remittances were USD 317 crore in January 2026 and 322 crore in December 2025, and below USD 3 billion in each of the five months before that.

Several bank officials said remittances usually rise before the two Eids; recently they rose mainly around the election, with most coming from countries with many Bangladeshis, and funds raised abroad for many candidates came in under the name of remittance.

key_quote_bn: চলতি ফেব্রুয়ারি মাসের প্রথম ১৬ দিনে দেশে ১৮০ কোটি ৭০ লাখ মার্কিন ডলারের রেমিট্যান্স বা প্রবাসী আয় এসেছে, যা গত বছরের একই বছরের সময়ের তুলনায় ২১ শতাংশ বেশি।

headline_en: BDT 1,550 crore a day in remittances before the vote
summary_en: In the first 9 days of February 2026 expatriates sent USD 113.5 crore (BDT 13,960 crore), 32.3% more than a year earlier, an average of BDT 1,550 crore a day. Because banks were closed for four days for the election and inter-bank transfers and mobile financial services were restricted, recipients could withdraw remittance only through ATM cards.

facts.statement: In the first 9 days of February 2026 expatriates sent USD 113 crore 50 lakh, equal to BDT 13,960 crore (an average of BDT 1,550 crore a day), 32.3% more than the USD 86 crore 60 lakh of the first 9 days of February 2025.
Remittances were USD 317 crore in January 2026 and 322 crore in December 2025; in each of the five months before that they were under USD 3 billion.

Several bank officials said remittances normally rise before the two Eids but were now rising mainly around the election; most comes from countries with many expatriate Bangladeshis, and funds collected abroad for many candidates are coming in the name of remittance.

In 2025 Bangladesh received USD 3,282 crore in remittances, about equal to the current foreign exchange reserves held at Bangladesh Bank; there was no real dollar shortage in 2025 and Bangladesh Bank bought dollars from banks throughout the year.

Because banks were closed for four consecutive days for the February 2026 election, remittance recipients could not withdraw money from bank branches; those with ATM cards could still withdraw, and depending on the bank up to BDT 2 lakh can be withdrawn from an ATM booth.

For the February 2026 election, transfers from one bank account to an account in another bank were suspended and mobile financial services (MFS) were limited, so remittance could not be withdrawn through bKash, Rocket, Nagad or other mobile banking services either.

key_quote_bn: তবে যাঁদের এটিএম কার্ড আছে, তাঁরা ঠিকই টাকা তুলতে পারছেন। এখন ব্যাংক ভেদে এটিএম বুথ থেকে ২ লাখ টাকা পর্যন্ত উত্তোলন করা যায়।

headline_en: Remittances equal to BDT 6,000 crore arrived in the first four days
summary_en: In the first four days of February 2026 Bangladesh received USD 50.6 crore (BDT 6,173 crore) in remittances, 19.8% more than a year earlier. The article lists monthly figures from July 2025 to January 2026 and bank officials' view that election spending is driving the rise.

facts.statement: In the first four days of February 2026 Bangladesh received USD 50 crore 60 lakh in remittances, equal to BDT 6,173 crore, 19.8% more than the USD 42 crore 20 lakh of the first four days of February 2025.

Monthly remittances: July 2025 USD 248 crore, August 242 crore, September 269 crore, October 256 crore, November 289 crore (highest of those five sub-3-billion months), December 322 crore, January 2026 317 crore.

Several bank officials said remittances usually rise before the two Eids but were now rising mainly because of the election, coming in to meet candidates' election expenses and from funds raised abroad for candidates; they expected the trend to last until the election.

In 2025 Bangladesh received USD 3,282 crore in remittances, about equal to the current reserves at Bangladesh Bank; Bangladesh Bank bought dollars from banks throughout the year to keep the market stable, which raised reserves.

key_quote_bn: চলতি মাসের প্রথম চার দিনে ৫০ কোটি ৬০ লাখ ডলার অর্থাৎ ৬ হাজার ১৭৩ কোটি টাকার সমপরিমাণ প্রবাসী আয় এসেছে।

headline_en: Remittances exceeded 3 billion dollars in the month before the vote
summary_en: Bangladesh received USD 317 crore in remittances in January 2026, according to Bangladesh Bank spokesperson Arif Hossain Khan on 1 February 2026. Bank officials said the pre-election rise is driven by candidates' election spending; the article repeats monthly figures and the hundi explanation.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 3.17 billion (317 crore) in remittances in January 2026.
facts.source_in_article: Arif Hossain Khan, executive director and spokesperson of Bangladesh Bank, 1 February 2026

facts.statement: Several bank officials told Prothom Alo that remittances were coming to meet various candidates' election expenses, mostly from countries with many expatriate Bangladeshis, including funds raised abroad for candidates that enter as remittance; they expected this to continue until the election.
December 2025 remittances were USD 322 crore, the second highest for a single month; the record then was USD 329 crore in March 2025, when expatriates sent more for Eid-ul-Fitr.

headline_en: Remittances up before the vote; USD 294 crore arrived in January
summary_en: In the first 28 days of January 2026 Bangladesh received about USD 294 crore in remittances, 50.6% more than a year earlier, and USD 1,921 crore since July 2025. The article also traces reserves from the 2021 peak of USD 48 billion to USD 32.26 billion now and the dollar rate from BDT 128 to BDT 122-123.

facts.statement: In the first 28 days of January 2026 Bangladesh received remittances the article prints as 'USD 294 crore 30' (২৯৪ কোটি ৩০ ডলার; headline says 294 crore), 50.6% more than the USD 195 crore 50 lakh of the first 28 days of January 2025.
From July 2025 to 28 January 2026 (fiscal 2025-26) Bangladesh received USD 1,921 crore in remittances, 22% more than the USD 1,573 crore of the same period of the previous fiscal year.

Several bank officials said remittances were rising mainly around the election, to meet candidates' election expenses and from funds raised abroad for candidates, and expected the trend to continue until the election.

Remittances were USD 248 crore in July 2025, 242 crore in August, 269 crore in September, 256 crore in October, 289 crore in November and 322 crore in December 2025; calendar 2025 totalled USD 3,282 crore.

During the dollar crisis the bank-sector dollar price rose as high as BDT 128; by late January 2026 the dollar was trading between BDT 122 and 123.

headline_en: What stands in the way of becoming a trillion-dollar economy
summary_en: An opinion column by Dr Mohammad Nuruzzaman, CEO of Daffodil Group Ltd, arguing that Bangladesh should plan skills, overseas and domestic jobs, formal remittances and returnee reintegration together to create 10 million jobs in 2026-2030. He proposes demand-led skilling, turning embassies into labour-market intelligence units, a private skill development board under NSDA, compulsory destination-language training and upskilling madrasa graduates for Arab labour markets.

facts.statement: The columnist says the skills most in demand in the global labour market are human care workers, construction and infrastructure skills, electrical and welding trades, manufacturing and factory technicians, hospitality and service sector, and digital and remote services.
facts.source_in_article: Dr Mohammad Nuruzzaman, CEO, Daffodil Group Ltd (opinion)

facts.statement: The columnist sees real opportunities for Bangladesh in care and technical skills for ageing populations in Japan and Europe, manufacturing skills in East Asia, construction and services in the Middle East, and remote work in the global digital economy, and calls for demand-led skilling (identify demand first, train afterwards).

The columnist proposes turning Bangladesh's foreign missions and embassies into labour market intelligence units that work with local employers, chambers of commerce and trade bodies to build pipelines of legal jobs, which he says would reduce dependence on brokers and make overseas employment more transparent and safe.

The columnist says the National Skills Development Authority (NSDA) has limited capacity, staff and regulatory power, and that Bangladesh has thousands of small training centres many of which are uneven in quality and effectively unregulated; he proposes a Private Skill Development Board under NSDA for curriculum standardisation, trainer qualification checks, outcome-based accreditation and regular evaluation.

The columnist proposes 'train the trainers' programmes that turn skilled returnee workers, experienced technicians and industry professionals into trainers, because the trainer shortage is the biggest obstacle to skilling 10 million people.

The columnist says language skill is one of the biggest multipliers of income in the international labour market: for Japan, Korea, Germany or Arab countries knowing the language makes getting a job easier and raises pay significantly, so country-specific language training should be made compulsory alongside skills training.

The columnist says many madrasa-educated youths have basic Arabic but lack modern vocational skills; targeted upskilling in care, service, construction and hospitality could connect them quickly to Arab countries' labour markets, with higher retention because of cultural and linguistic fit.

The columnist says a large share of remittances still flows through informal or hundi channels and proposes, besides the cash incentive, tax breaks, faster service, priority loans for returnee entrepreneurs and easier digital transactions for remittances sent through formal banking and digital channels.

The columnist claims that if returnee workers are turned into SME entrepreneurs in a planned way, one worker can create three to five new jobs; he puts Bangladesh's youth population at close to 6 crore and the economy at about USD 450 billion.

named_actors.name: Dr Mohammad Nuruzzaman
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Chief executive officer of Daffodil Group Ltd; author of the opinion column.

headline_en: Remittances pass 2 billion dollars in 21 days
summary_en: In the first 21 days of January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 233.1 crore in remittances, about 55% more than a year earlier, as the election approached. Bank officials told Prothom Alo that most of the extra inflow is being sent to cover candidates' election costs and expect good inflows until March.

facts.statement: In the first 21 days of January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 233 crore 10 lakh in remittances, about 55% more than the same period a year earlier; in the preceding week the daily average was USD 11 crore 10 lakh, and USD 11 crore came on 21 January.
From July 2025 to 21 January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 1,859 crore in remittances against USD 1,528 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal year, growth of 21.7%.
Remittances were USD 322 crore in December 2025 and about 289 crore in November 2025, a rise of USD 33 crore; calendar 2025 totalled USD 3,282 crore, about equal to current reserves.

Several bank officials told Prothom Alo that a large part of the extra remittance now arriving is being sent to meet candidates' election expenses, including funds raised abroad for candidates; with the election and Ramadan they expect good remittance inflows until March 2026.

Reserves peaked at USD 48 billion in 2021, were about USD 25.58 billion when the Awami League government fell in August 2024, and had risen to USD 32 billion (3,200 crore) by January 2026; the dollar, which had reached BDT 128 in the banking sector, was trading at BDT 122 to 123.

key_quote_bn: একাধিক ব্যাংক কর্মকর্তা প্রথম আলোকে জানান, এখন বাড়তি যে প্রবাসী আয় আসছে, তার বড় অংশই বিভিন্ন প্রার্থীর নির্বাচনের খরচ মেটানোর জন্য পাঠানো হচ্ছে।

headline_en: BDT 1,500 crore in remittances arriving every day
summary_en: In the first 14 days of January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 170.3 crore in remittances, about 69.8% more than a year earlier, averaging USD 12.16 crore (about BDT 1,500 crore) a day. Bank officials attribute most of the extra inflow to candidates' election spending.

facts.statement: In the first 14 days of January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 170 crore 30 lakh in remittances, about 69.8% more than the same period a year earlier, a daily average of USD 12 crore 16 lakh or roughly BDT 1,500 crore; USD 11 crore 30 lakh came on 14 January.
From July 2025 to 14 January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 1,796 crore in remittances against USD 1,478 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal year, growth of 21.6%.
Remittances were USD 322 crore in December 2025 and about 289 crore in November 2025; calendar 2025 totalled USD 3,282 crore.

Several bank officials told Prothom Alo that a large part of the extra remittance is being sent for candidates' election expenses, including funds raised abroad for candidates, and that with the election and Ramadan good inflows will continue until March 2026.

Reserves peaked at USD 48 billion in 2021, fell to USD 26 billion at the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024, and were USD 32 billion (3,200 crore) in mid-January 2026; the dollar had reached BDT 128 and was trading at BDT 122-123.

headline_en: Remittances buoyant before the vote
summary_en: In the first seven days of January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 90.7 crore in remittances, 68% more than a year earlier, as the national election and Ramadan approached. Banks have surplus dollars and Bangladesh Bank bought USD 20.6 crore from 15 banks at BDT 122.30; reserves stood at USD 32.43 billion after the ACU payment.

facts.statement: In the first seven days of January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 90 crore 70 lakh in remittances, 68% more than the first 7 days of the previous year.

Several bank officials told Prothom Alo that a large part of the extra remittance is being sent to cover candidates' election expenses, including funds raised abroad for candidates entering as remittance; they expect good inflows until March 2026 with the election and Ramadan.
December 2025 remittances were USD 322 crore, the second-highest single month after USD 329 crore in March 2025 (Eid-ul-Fitr); calendar 2025 totalled USD 3,282 crore.
From July 2025 to 7 January 2026 Bangladesh received USD 17.17 billion (1,717 crore) in remittances, against USD 14.31 billion from July 2024 to 7 January 2025, about 20% more.

With banks holding surplus dollars, Bangladesh Bank bought USD 20 crore 60 lakh from 15 banks on Thursday (8 January 2026) at BDT 122.30 per dollar; the article says its dollar purchases in the first six months of the fiscal year reached USD 375 crore, of which USD 61 crore was in January.
After paying a USD 153 crore Asian Clearing Union (ACU) bill in January 2026, Bangladesh's reserves were USD 32.43 billion (USD 27.84 billion under IMF BPM6).

Reserves peaked at USD 48 billion in 2021 and fell to USD 26 billion at the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024, when the dollar reached BDT 128 in banks; by January 2026 it had fallen to BDT 122.

Banking sector people say remittances have stayed positive since the fall of the Awami League government on 5 August 2024 because money laundering and therefore illegal hundi business fell and the banking-channel exchange rate has been stable for several months.

headline_en: Krishi Bank keeps second place in remittances; three banks brought 37%
summary_en: Bangladesh received USD 3,282 crore in remittances in 2025, of which three banks, Islami Bank, Bangladesh Krishi Bank and Agrani Bank, brought 36.91%. The article gives the 2025 figures for the top ten banks and bankers' reasons for the rise: the 2.5% cash incentive, a market-based exchange rate narrowing the gap with hundi, and bank links with bKash, Nagad and Rocket.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received a total of USD 3,282 crore in remittances in calendar 2025.

In 2025 expatriates sent USD 620 crore 40 lakh through Islami Bank Bangladesh (first), USD 312 crore 70 lakh through Bangladesh Krishi Bank (BKB, second) and USD 278 crore 20 lakh through Agrani Bank (third); together these three brought 36.91% of the year's remittances.

Other banks' 2025 remittance collection: Janata Bank USD 225 crore 70 lakh (fourth), BRAC Bank 217 crore 10 lakh, Trust Bank 181 crore 60 lakh, Sonali Bank 151 crore 30 lakh, Rupali Bank 121 crore 50 lakh, City Bank 95 crore 10 lakh and Bank Asia 84 crore 80 lakh.
The single-month remittance record as of early January 2026 was USD 329 crore in March 2025; December 2025 again exceeded USD 300 crore.

Banking sector people said the government-declared 2.5% cash incentive on remittances, together with making the dollar exchange rate market-based, has narrowed the price gap between hundi and the banking channel, encouraging expatriates to send money through banks instead of taking the risk of hundi.

Because commercial banks are interconnected with mobile financial services such as bKash, Nagad and Rocket, remittance money reaches the family within a short time, which the article says is a big attraction for expatriates.
By Bangladesh Bank's account the country's foreign exchange reserves stood at USD 3,300 crore in early January 2026.
Bank officials attribute the rise in remittances to reduced money laundering cutting illegal hundi business and to a banking-channel exchange rate that has been stable for several months.

key_quote_bn: সরকার ঘোষিত আড়াই শতাংশ নগদ প্রণোদনার পাশাপাশি ডলারের বিনিময় হার বাজারভিত্তিক করার ফলে হুন্ডি ও ব্যাংকিং চ্যানেলের দামের ব্যবধান কমে এসেছে।

headline_en: Remittances in one year equal to the reserves
summary_en: Bangladesh received USD 322 crore in remittances in December 2025, the second-highest month after March 2025, and USD 3,282 crore in all of 2025, about equal to Bangladesh Bank's reserves. Reserves passed USD 33 billion at year end as Bangladesh Bank bought dollars from banks at BDT 122.30.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 322 crore in remittances in December 2025, the second-highest single month after the record USD 329 crore of March 2025, and USD 33 crore more than November 2025's roughly 289 crore.
In the whole of 2025 Bangladesh received USD 3,282 crore in remittances, about equal to Bangladesh Bank's foreign exchange holdings.
Sector people said remittances rose in December 2025 around the coming national election.
Gross reserves passed USD 33 billion at the end of 2025, the highest in three years; at the end of Tuesday (30 December 2025) they were USD 3,318 crore, or USD 2,851 crore under IMF BPM6.

On Tuesday (30 December 2025) Bangladesh Bank bought USD 8 crore 90 lakh from seven banks by auction at BDT 122.30 per dollar; the article says its purchases in the first six months of fiscal 2025-26 totalled USD 3.13 billion (313 crore), over USD 1 billion of it in December alone.

Reserves peaked at USD 48 billion in 2021 and fell to USD 26 billion at the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024, when the dollar reached BDT 128 in banks; it had fallen to BDT 122 by the end of 2025.
Banking sector people attribute the rise in remittances since August 2024 to lower money laundering reducing illegal hundi and a banking-channel dollar rate stable for several months.

key_quote_bn: বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকের তথ্য অনুযায়ী, ২০২৫ সালের পুরো বছরে দেশে প্রবাসী আয় এসেছিল ৩ হাজার ২৮২ কোটি ডলার।

headline_en: Remittances pass 2 billion dollars in just 17 days
summary_en: In the first 17 days of December 2025 remittances passed USD 200 crore, 14% more than a year earlier, and reserves reached USD 32.57 billion. Governor Ahsan H. Mansur said reserves would reach USD 34-35 billion by end-December by buying dollars domestically rather than through IMF loans.

facts.statement: From 1 to 17 December 2025 Bangladesh received remittances the article prints as 'USD 200 crore 7' (২০০ কোটি ৭ ডলার), against USD 176 crore in the same days of 2024, a rise of 14%; USD 17 crore 70 lakh came on 17 December.

From July to 17 December 2025 Bangladesh received USD 1,505 crore in remittances against USD 1,290 crore in the same period a year earlier, a rise of 16.7%; November 2025 brought USD 288 crore 95 lakh.
Bangladesh received USD 3,033 crore in remittances in fiscal 2024-25 and USD 2,391 crore in fiscal 2023-24; in July-October 2025 about USD 2.5 billion came each month.
Bangladesh Bank's foreign exchange reserves were USD 32.57 billion (3,257 crore) on Thursday 18 December 2025.

Bangladesh Bank Governor Ahsan H. Mansur said at an event on Thursday 18 December 2025 that reserves would reach USD 34-35 billion by the end of December and would be built by buying dollars from within the country, not through loans from the IMF or any agency.
facts.source_in_article: Ahsan H. Mansur, Governor, Bangladesh Bank

facts.statement: Bangladesh Bank officials said government and central bank initiatives against hundi and the incentive have played a big role in increasing remittances through the banking channel.
The single-month record as of December 2025 was USD 329 crore in March 2025; no month after that had exceeded USD 300 crore until December 2025, which bankers expected might do so.

key_quote_bn: বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকের কর্মকর্তারা বলছেন, হুন্ডি প্রতিরোধে সরকার ও কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংকের উদ্যোগ, প্রণোদনা ব্যাংকিং চ্যানেলে প্রবাসী আয় বাড়াতে বড় ভূমিকা রেখেছে।

headline_en: Krishi Bank's big surprise in remittances
summary_en: Bangladesh Krishi Bank ranked second in collecting remittances in January-November 2025 (USD 277 crore), behind Islami Bank (USD 553 crore) and ahead of Agrani Bank (USD 265 crore). The article explains how the bank used its 1,038-branch rural network, agreements with foreign money-transfer firms, NGOs and MFS providers, expatriate savings schemes and round-the-clock direct account credit to grow, and names the transfer firms it gets most from.

facts.statement: In January-November 2025 Bangladesh received USD 2,958 crore in remittances, of which ten banks brought USD 2,063 crore (70%): Islami Bank 553 crore, Krishi Bank 277 crore, Agrani 265 crore, Janata 197 crore, BRAC Bank 191 crore, Trust Bank 160 crore, Sonali 145 crore, Rupali 110 crore, City 84 crore and Pubali 79 crore.

Bangladesh Krishi Bank has 1,038 branches and 5 sub-branches across the country, the widest network including remote areas of any bank; it has appointed Rajshahi Krishi Unnayan Bank as sub-agent in the northern region so it can provide remittance service across the whole country.

Other banks and mobile financial service providers formerly used Krishi Bank's network to distribute remittances for a small fee; after Ali Hossain Prodhania joined as managing director in 2018 the bank signed agreements with foreign money-transfer companies to use the network for itself.
During the coronavirus outbreak Krishi Bank kept all branches open and distributed remittances, which made it popular among expatriates.
Krishi Bank has launched several savings schemes for expatriates, in which about BDT 220 crore has been deposited.

Expatriates deposit money at money-transfer companies abroad and Bangladeshi banks collect remittances from those companies; money a bank collects for accounts outside itself is sent on to the relevant bank's account the same day.

Krishi Bank gets the most remittance from Merchantrade of Malaysia, followed by Instant Cash and Ria Money of the United States, CBL Money and NBL Money of Malaysia, Western Union, NEC Money of the United Kingdom, Home Remit of South Africa and EZ Remit of the United Kingdom.

Krishi Bank's general manager for international and accounts, Mostafizur Rahman, said customers earlier mainly received remittance using a secret PIN number, but now with greater financial inclusion they can have money credited directly to their own accounts, a service given 24 hours through Bangladesh Bank.
facts.source_in_article: Mostafizur Rahman, General Manager (International and Accounts), Bangladesh Krishi Bank

facts.statement: Mostafizur Rahman said Krishi Bank's agreements with MFS providers including bKash and Nagad and with important money exchange houses have made the service easier; its biggest strength is more than a thousand branches in remote areas.

Krishi Bank was tasked by the government during the dollar crisis with opening letters of credit for power, fuel and food imports and now pays USD 20-25 crore a month of government import liabilities, meeting the dollar demand from remittances; it earned about BDT 700 crore from foreign exchange business last fiscal year, targets BDT 1,000 crore this fiscal year, and had a loss of BDT 6,513 crore in fiscal 2023-24.
Krishi Bank signed agreements with NGOs under which NGOs can deposit the money they collect at any Krishi Bank branch free of charge and transfer it to their own bank.

named_actors.name: Ali Hossain Prodhania

key_quote_bn: এখন আর্থিক অন্তর্ভুক্তি বাড়ায় গ্রাহকেরা নিজের হিসাবে সরাসরি টাকা জমা নিতে পারছেন।

headline_en: USD 289 crore in remittances came in November
summary_en: Expatriates sent USD 288.9 crore in November 2025, about 31.38% more than November 2024. The article gives the bank-category breakdown, the fiscal year-to-date total and the reserve position.

facts.statement: Expatriates sent USD 288 crore 90 lakh to Bangladesh in November 2025, USD 69 crore more than the USD 219 crore 90 lakh of November 2024, growth of about 31.38%.
In November 2025 the six state-owned banks brought USD 58 crore 70 lakh in remittances, Krishi Bank USD 29 crore 59 lakh, private banks USD 199 crore 68 lakh and foreign banks USD 59 lakh.
From 1 July to 30 November 2025 (fiscal 2025-26) Bangladesh received USD 1,303 crore in remittances.
Bangladesh received USD 3,033 crore in remittances in fiscal 2024-25 and USD 2,391 crore in fiscal 2023-24; July-October 2025 brought about USD 2.5 billion a month.
The article says Bangladesh Bank's gross reserves exceeded '31 billion or 3,200 crore dollars' (the two figures as printed do not match); under IMF BPM6 they were a little over USD 26 billion.

The reason given for higher remittances is that illegal hundi business has shrunk as money laundering fell and the banking-channel dollar rate is stable; bank officials said that with good remittance inflows there is no problem opening letters of credit for imports.

headline_en: Remittances up 31 percent in the first 18 days of the month
summary_en: In the first 18 days of November 2025 Bangladesh received USD 190 crore in remittances, 31% more than the USD 146 crore of the same days in 2024. From 1 July to 18 November 2025 the total was USD 1,205 crore, 15.9% up.

facts.statement: In the first 18 days of November 2025 Bangladesh received USD 190 crore in remittances, 31% more than the USD 146 crore of the first 18 days of November 2024.

From 1 July to 18 November 2025 Bangladesh received USD 1,205 crore in remittances, up 15.9%; the article gives the year-earlier comparison as USD 1,040 crore but labels it 'export income' (রপ্তানি আয়) in the text.
Bangladesh received USD 3,033 crore in remittances in fiscal 2024-25 and USD 2,391 crore in fiscal 2023-24; in each of the two months before November 2025 about USD 2.5 billion came.
Bangladesh Bank's gross reserves recently exceeded USD 32 billion (3,200 crore) but stood at USD 31 billion at the time of the article (21 November 2025).

headline_en: Bangladesh to take steps to help fill Japan's shortage of 11 million workers
summary_en: The Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo, with JITCO, held a seminar and matching event in Nagoya on Friday 7 November 2025 on Bangladesh as a source of skilled workers for Japan, attended by about 250 sending and recruiting organisations. Senior Secretary Neyamat Ullah Bhuiyan said 33 technical training centres have been designated for the Japanese market and a 'Japan Cell' formed in the expatriates' welfare ministry; four MoUs and agreements were signed.

facts.statement: On Friday 7 November 2025 the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo held a seminar titled 'Bangladesh: a highly promising source of skilled human resources for Japan' and then a matching event in an auditorium in Nagoya, Japan, in cooperation with the Japan International Trainee and Skilled Worker Cooperation Organization (JITCO); about 250 manpower exporting firms and recruiting organisations took part.

Senior Secretary Neyamat Ullah Bhuiyan of the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment said Japan will need about 1 crore 10 lakh (11 million) foreign workers by 2040, while Bangladesh currently has a surplus working-age population of 2 crore 50 lakh, a trend that will continue until 2040; he pledged all steps to help fill Japan's shortage.
facts.source_in_article: Neyamat Ullah Bhuiyan, Senior Secretary, Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment

facts.statement: The Senior Secretary said 33 Technical Training Centres in Bangladesh have been designated to prepare workers according to the demand of Japan's labour market, and the number will be increased if needed.
The Senior Secretary said a 'Japan Cell' has been formed in the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare to act as the coordination and communication centre for the Japanese labour market.
At the Nagoya event four memoranda of understanding and agreements were signed between Bangladeshi manpower sending organisations and Japanese recruiting organisations.

Bangladesh's ambassador to Japan, Md. Daud Ali, promised all kinds of support from the embassy for sending skilled workers to Japan; JITCO senior vice president Shigeo Matsutomi gave a presentation on the international labour market and the prospects of Japan's labour market.

headline_en: The youth who hired a loudspeaker to abuse villagers after failing to go abroad is getting his wish
summary_en: Sarwar Hossain (27) of Hossainpur, Kishoreganj, had a visa for Saudi Arabia but could not raise the money or get a bank loan, and on 16 October 2025 hired a loudspeaker to abuse his neighbours; the video went viral. After media reports, Probashi Kallyan Bank's Kishoreganj branch verified his papers and gave him a BDT 2 lakh loan, repayable in instalments starting after two months; he was due to fly on 30 October 2025.

facts.statement: Probashi Kallyan Bank's Kishoreganj branch gave Sarwar Hossain (27), who had a visa for Saudi Arabia but no money to travel, a loan of BDT 2 lakh after verification of his papers; he will repay in instalments starting two months later.
facts.source_in_article: Mozammel Haque, General Manager, Probashi Kallyan Bank, Kishoreganj branch

facts.statement: Sarwar Hossain said that after media reports the Kishoreganj branch of Probashi Kallyan Bank phoned him, verified his documents and then gave him the BDT 2 lakh loan; he bought his ticket and was due to go to Saudi Arabia on 30 October 2025.

Sarwar Hossain of Dakshin Panan village, Gobindapur union, Hossainpur upazila, Kishoreganj, from a poor family, had tried repeatedly and failed to get a bank loan (he believed because neighbours did not cooperate) and appeals to NGOs and others also failed; on 16 October 2025 he hired a loudspeaker for BDT 500 and abused the villagers, then posted the video on Facebook himself.
